title: Lucifer Yellow - A Robust Paracellular Permeability Marker in a Cell Model of the Human Blood-brain Barrier
protocol: Add 8.5 mL of collagen solution in a T75 tissue culture flask.
Place the flask in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Remove the collagen solution from the flask.
Gently wash the flask with sterilized phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Add 15 mL of complete growth medium to the flask.
Leave the flask in the CO2 incubator for 15 minutes.
Move a cryovial of frozen hCMEC/D3 cells from the liquid nitrogen tank and rapidly thaw it in a 37 °C water bath (< 1 min).
Aspirate and transfer the thawed cells to the flask containing pre-warmed medium.
Gently shake the flask to mix the cells with the growth medium.
Place the flask in the incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Observe the cells under a light microscope after 2 hours to ensure they are attached.
Remove the old growth medium once the cells attach.
Add 10 mL of fresh pre-warmed growth medium to replace dimethylsulfoxide in the old medium.
Check under a light microscope after 24 hours for spindle-shaped cells.
Replace the old growth medium with pre-warmed fresh growth medium.
Replenish the growth medium every other day until confluence is reached.
Check the cells under the microscope before removing the old growth medium.
Examine hCMEC/D3 cells under phase contrast microscope to ensure they appear healthy.
Remove old growth medium from the flask.
Transfer 10 mL of pre-warmed fresh medium into the flask, avoiding direct contact with the cell surface.
Turn the flask back into horizontal position and gently rock it several times.
Check hCMEC/D3 cells under the microscope before returning the flask to the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2).
Observe the cells under an inverted light microscope each time before and after handling the cells.
Record any noticeable changes in cell number or morphology in the laboratory notebook.
Incubate a new T75 flask with 8.5 mL of collagen solution for 1 h in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2).
Remove the collagen solution from the flask.
Gently wash the flask with sterilized PBS.
Add 10 mL of pre-warmed hCMEC/D3 medium to the new flask.
Place the flask in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2).
Take out the flask from the incubator.
Examine hCMEC/D3 cells under a phase contrast microscope to check if the cells are 100% confluent.
Remove hCMEC/D3 cell medium from the flask containing cells.
Wash hCMEC/D3 cells with 10 mL of PBS.
Add 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin solution containing 0.02% EDTA to the flask.
Trypsinize for 2-5 min in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2).
Tap the flask gently on the sides to help detachment.
Never leave the cells on trypsin/EDTA for more than 6 min.
Add 10 mL of pre-warmed hCMEC/D3 medium to stop trypsinization.
Resuspend hCMEC/D3 cells by pipetting up and down several times.
Transfer the entire cell suspension from the flask into a 15 mL tube.
Transfer 1 mL of the cell suspension to a new flask with pre-warmed fresh medium.
Return the new flask to the incubator.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down several times before transferring to minimize concentration gradients.
Place tissue culture inserts with microporous membranes (pore size: 0.4 µm, material: PET) into a 24-well culture plate.
Add 400 µL of collagen type I (0.15 mg/mL) in each tissue culture insert.
Incubate the inserts for 1 hour in a CO2 incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Rock the 24-well plate gently to allow even spreading of the collagen solution over the microporous membrane.
Remove the collagen solution from the inserts.
Gently wash the microporous membrane with 0.4 mL of 1x PBS buffer.
Plate hCMEC/D3 cells at a density of 50,000 cells/cm² in the cell inserts (15,000 cells in 500 µL of medium).
Resuspend the cell suspension with a 10 mL pipette before adding cells to the inserts to minimize differences in cell number.
Place the 24-well plate with tissue culture setup in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Incubate the plate for 7 days to allow cells to reach 100% confluency.
Remove growth medium every other day.
Transfer 0.5 mL of pre-warmed fresh media into tissue culture inserts.
Repeat the plating procedure on a 12-well plate, 48-well plate, and 96-well plate.
Use the 12-well plate for Western blotting to determine changes in ZO-1 expression.
Use the 48-well plate for DNA NP transfection.
Use the 96-well plate for the ATP assay to determine cell viability in transfected cells.
Seed cells at a density of 50,000 cell/cm² in a collagen-coated 24-well tissue culture plate.
Remove growth medium on each day of the experiment.
Gently wash the cells twice with 500 µL of 1x PBS.
Add 30 µL of 0.25% trypsin solution containing 0.02% EDTA.
Leave the plate for about 2-5 min in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO₂).
Increase volumes of trypsin/EDTA as indicated: 30 µL for 1-5 days post-seeding, 60 µL for 6-7 days post-seeding, and 100 µL for 8-10 days post-seeding.
Add either 470 µL, 440 µL, or 400 µL of growth medium based on the volume of trypsin/EDTA solution added to prepare 500 µL of cell suspension in each well.
Suspend the cells by pipetting up and down in each well several times.
Observe the cells under a microscope to ensure all cells are suspended in the growth medium.
If some cells are still attached, gently scrape the cells using a plastic cell scraper.
Remove 0.1 mL of cell suspension from 500 µL cell suspension.
Add 0.1 mL of 0.4% Trypan blue solution to the cell suspension and mix well.
Clean a hemacytometer with 70% isopropyl alcohol.
Add 20 µL of mixture on each side in the V-groove of the hemacytometer.
Locate two random grids on each side of the hemacytometer under the microscope.
Count all living, non-blue cells within the grids.
Calculate the average number of cells per grid using the provided formula.
Determine the dilution factor using the given equation.
Calculate the cell density (viable cells/cm²) based on the provided formula.
Add 8.3 μL of the transfection formulation mixed with 50 μL of complete growth medium and incubate for 4 h.
Gently wash the apical side twice using sterile 1x PBS buffer.
Aspirate residual reagents and medium to minimize cell detachment.
Remove the growth medium.
Add 1.5 mL of pre-warmed transport buffer to the basolateral side.
Add 58.3 μL of 20 μM LY solution to the apical side.
Save 50 μL of the 20 μM LY solution for fluorescence measurements.
Incubate in a rotary plate shaker at 37 °C and 100 rpm for 60 min.
Remove 30 μL of the LY sample from each apical compartment.
Transfer the 20 µM LY solution to pre-labeled tubes.
Dilute the 20 µM LY stock solution 10-fold using transport buffer.
Transfer 500 μL from each basolateral compartment to pre-labeled tubes.
Prepare a series of LY standards for the standard curve.
Add 100 µL of each standard in duplicate, apical and basolateral samples to each well in a black 96-well plate.
Measure the LY fluorescence intensity using a fluorescence microplate reader set at excitation 428 nm and emission 536 nm.
Remove the growth medium from the transwell inserts and 12-well plate.
Gently wash the apical side and 12-well plate using pre-warmed calcium-free medium (Minimum Essential Medium Eagle Spinner (S-MEM) medium).
Add 500 µL or 2 mL of pre-warmed S-MEM 1xmedium to the inserts or 12-well plate.
Incubate for 24 h in the incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Remove the S-MEM 1x medium after incubation.
Wash the cells once using pre-warmed 1x PBS buffer.
Dilute the stock solution of gWIZ-Luc plasmid in 10 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH 5.0).
Allow the DNA solution to stand for 10 min at room temperature.
Thaw the frozen gWIZ-Luc plasmid stock completely on ice.
Gently vortex the diluted DNA stock solution for 30 s on a standard benchtop vortexer set at knob position 3-5.
Calculate the desired N/P ratios.
Seed the cells with the density of 50,000 cell/cm² in a 48 well plate and grow until confluence in the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO₂).
Mix 25 µL of the indicated sample (transfection formulation) with 150 µL of complete growth medium.
Add 175 µL of this mixture to each well.
Observe the hCMEC/D3 cells under a microscope to ensure they appear healthy and are 100% confluent at the time of the experiment.
Remove the growth medium from wells.
Add 175 µL transfection mixture to each well.
Incubate the plate for 4 h at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Remove the transfection mixture after incubation.
Wash hCMEC/D3 cells with pre-warmed sterile 1x PBS buffer carefully along the walls of the wells.
Gently rock the plate a few times to minimize cell detachment during washing.
Discard the PBS wash and add 500 µL of pre-warmed culture medium.
Incubate for 24 h at 37 °C in the incubator.
Remove growth medium completely after 24 h.
Wash cells once with pre-warmed 1x PBS.
Add 100 µL of ice-cold luciferase cell culture lysis reagent per well to lyse the cells.
Add 20 µL of cell lysate and 100 µL of luciferase assay buffer into a 1.5 mL tube.
Read the luminescence of the sample on a Luminometer with a Single Auto-injector, integrating over 10 s before reading.
Measure the total amount of cellular protein in the lysate using a bicinchoninic acid assay kit according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Calculate and express luciferase gene expression as Relative Light Units per total cellular protein.
Seed cells at a density of 50,000 cell/cm² in a 96 well plate and grow until confluence in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO₂).
Transfect the cells with 9.7 µL of transfection formulation and 58.4 µL of complete growth medium for 4 h.
Remove the transfection mixture and gently wash the cells twice with pre-warmed PBS buffer to remove treatment reagents completely.
Mix 75 µL of fresh pre-warmed medium and ATP assay reagent in a 1:1 dilution using a multichannel pipette.
Place the plate on a nutating shaker for 15 min at room temperature.
Transfer 60 µL of each sample into a white 96-well plate.
Pop any air bubbles using a needle prior to reading the plate.
Read the plate on a luminometer with a 1 s integration time.
Read the plate within 20 min after adding ATP assay reagents.
Calculate the percent (%) cell viability using this formula: (luminescence of transfected cells/luminescence of control, untreated cells) x 100.
Seed the cells at a density of 50,000 cell/cm² in a collagen-coated 12-well tissue culture plate.
On day 3, day 5, day 7, and day 10 post-seeding, remove the growth medium and gently wash the cells twice with 2 mL of ice-cold 1x PBS.
Add 300 µL mixture of ice-cold 1x RIPA lysis buffer containing 3 µg/mL aprotinin in each well.
Perform two freeze-thaw cycles (-80 °C).
Scrape the cells using a cold plastic cell scraper.
Collect the cell lysates in microfuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 200 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant into clean tubes and place them on ice.
Measure the total amount of cellular protein in the lysates using the BCA assay kit according to the manufacturer's protocol.

Denature aliquots of total homogenates containing 40 µg of total protein with 1x Laemmli buffer at 95 °C for 5 minutes and subject them to electrophoresis in a reducing 6-7.5% sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel (SDS-PAGE) at 90 V for 10 minutes through the stacking gel, then continue at 120 V.

Transfer the separated proteins onto a nitrocellulose membrane with pH 8.5 transfer buffer containing 192 mM Glycine, 25 mM Tris Base, 10% methanol, and 0.1% SDS at 75 V for 110 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the membrane using Tris-buffered saline containing 0.1% Tween 20 (T-TBS).
Block the membranes with a solution of 1:1 LiCOR-Odyssey Block and 1x Tris buffered saline for 60 minutes.
Carefully cut the membrane into two strips.
Incubate with ZO-1 monoclonal antibody at a dilution of 1:900 overnight at 4 °C.
Incubate with glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) antibody at a dilution of 1:10,000 overnight at 4 °C.
Incubate the ZO-1 membrane with donkey anti-mouse IgG at a dilution of 1:50,000.
Incubate the GAPDH membrane with donkey anti-mouse IgG at a dilution of 1:50,000.
Wash the membranes using T-TBS.
Image the ZO-1 and GAPDH membranes in the 700 channel on a 16-bit imager.
